features: THE THINGS THE PROGRAM SAID IT DID — This release adds nothing: it withdraws promises the software wasn't keeping. No migration, no change to the calculation engine, no new feature. It began with a precise question from an administrator on the forum — how does the software handle a cost approved before a sale, and heating consumed before a change of tenant — and the answer was an uncomfortable one: it doesn't handle them, and in seven places the screens said otherwise.

THE VALIDITY DATES DO NOT DO WHAT THE SCREENS PROMISED. On an ownership record you can enter a start date and an end date: they are saved, they are listed, and no calculation reads them. When the apportionment decides who to charge it looks at the role and an «active» flag, and nothing else — there is no per-day calculation anywhere in the program. The defect wasn't the missing feature but the sentences that presented it as present: «the system will know exactly when to stop charging the instalments», «automatically hand over to the new parties», «calculating the balances due for each period». Anyone who trusted them had been charging the seller for months without knowing.

SEVEN TEXTS REWRITTEN. They now say that the dates are recorded, that the apportionment does not use them, and that until it does a mid-year change of ownership must be worked out by hand. One promise that didn't even have a design phase — «handover notifications» — was removed rather than reworded.

A COMMAND TO TELL YOU WHETHER IT HAPPENED TO YOU. Correcting the wording tells nobody whether they were caught by it. The new `php artisan kondomanager:verifica-titolarita` lists, building by building, who filled in an end date believing it would stop the charges, the deactivated records that no screen can switch back on, and the units whose shares do not add up to 100. It is read-only: it says where to look, it changes nothing.

THAT LAST SIGNAL MEASURES A LOSS IN EUROS: two owners each at 100 % on the same unit normalise to 200 and pay half each — identical for a deed signed in January and one signed in December. It is how a change of ownership gets recorded today, because it is the only way the interface allows.

THE WATER TABLE WAS COLLECTING READINGS NOBODY USED. Choosing «Water» or «Heating» as the table type brought up five extra fields — meter, last reading, dispersion coefficient, fixed share, variable share. They were filled in, they were saved, and the apportionment never opened them: it divided on the column values like any other table. Anyone filling them in believed they were splitting by consumption and were splitting by thousandths.

THE FIVE FIELDS ARE GONE, THE TWO TABLE TYPES STAY — because they were not the problem. A «Water» table with «cubic metres» as its unit, where you enter each unit's consumption, already is a working consumption split. What was missing — meter management and the fixed/variable split of UNI 10200 — is a module planned for later, and the program no longer pretends to have it.

THE PRINTED APPORTIONMENT NO LONGER CONTRADICTS ITSELF AFTER A CHANGE OF OWNERSHIP. The workaround administrators use today is: generate the instalments, detach the former owner, reprint. Their shares remain in the charges but they are no longer in the thousandths table, and on the document all their cells came out as zero while the row total stayed correct: the row didn't add up to its own cells, and the columns didn't add up to the grand total — on the same sheet that goes to the meeting. That residual now lands in the «direct charge» column.

Under the hood: seven new tests. Also removed two fields that didn't really exist — a column declared in the code and absent from the database, and a value written on every save that no screen read and that was empty on every row.
